item.title: Gas Markets Manager at ICF (remote in US possible)
item.description: ICF is seeking a North American Natural Gas Markets subject matter expert (SME) and Manager to join the North American Natural Gas Markets team within the Energy Digital Infrastructure and Investment Line of Business.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
ICF is seeking a North American Natural Gas Markets subject matter expert (SME) and Manager to join the North American Natural Gas Markets team within the Energy Digital Infrastructure and Investment Line of Business. This role is for a hands-on natural gas market consultant and modeler who can connect rigorous quantitative analysis with clear, decision-ready advice for public- and private-sector clients.

The Manager will contribute directly to ICF’s quarterly North American Natural Gas Base Case long-term outlook and consulting engagements using ICF’s proprietary Gas Market Model (GMM) which is similar to the Gas Pipeline Competition Model (GPCM). Prior experience with GPCM is preferred. The successful candidate must bring strong regional experience with North American natural gas markets and understanding of market dynamics so they learn GMM quickly.

This is a balanced technical and client-facing role. The Manager will independently lead projects or major workstreams, guide analysts, communicate findings to clients, and collaborate with ICF colleagues across natural gas, power, economics, utilities, and investment advisory services.

Key responsibilities

  • Serve as a gas regional market expert and hands-on natural gas market modeler, developing assumptions and scenarios and translating model results into insights on prices, basis, supply, demand, pipeline flows, capacity utilization, storage, and infrastructure needs.

  • Learn and apply ICF’s proprietary GMM to run, maintain, calibrate, troubleshoot, document, and quality-check North American natural gas market forecasts; contribute to model and workflow improvements.

  • Lead a group of analysts that run and maintain GMM.

  • Support production of ICF’s quarterly North American Natural Gas Base Case and related subscription products.

  • Analyze North American natural gas fundamentals across production basins and demand sectors, including residential and commercial load, industrial demand, power generation, LNG exports, pipeline exports, and storage activity.

  • Evaluate pipeline and storage infrastructure, transportation constraints, regional basis formation, project timing, market need, utilization, reliability, and the effects of expansions or other market changes.

  • Lead or manage consulting workstreams involving market outlooks, scenario and risk analysis, pipeline and storage assessments, gas utility planning and supply portfolios, asset valuation and due diligence, regulatory and policy analysis, LNG, and gas-to-power or large-load development.

  • Design analytical approaches, manage schedules and budgets for assigned work, coordinate contributors, identify risks early, and deliver accurate reports, presentations, and quantitative models.

  • Present methods, results, uncertainties, and strategic implications clearly to clients and internal stakeholders; respond to technical questions with sound market judgment.

  • Mentor analysts and consultants through structured review, coaching, and knowledge transfer while remaining directly engaged in the technical work.

  • Collaborate across ICF to integrate natural gas analysis with power-market modeling, infrastructure advisory, economics, regulatory, and other related capabilities.

  • Contribute to proposals, scopes of work, client discussions, and thought leadership by helping shape technically sound approaches and communicating ICF’s capabilities.

Required qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in economics, engineering, energy, statistics, mathematics, data science, public policy, finance, or a related quantitative field.

  • 5+ years of relevant professional experience in North American natural gas fundamentals and market analysis, energy consulting, market research, a utility or a pipeline/midstream company, an upstream company, trading or commercial analytics, government, or a related field

  • Demonstrated experience using a natural gas market model or comparable quantitative market-forecasting framework to evaluate supply, demand, transportation, storage, prices, basis, or infrastructure scenarios.

  • Experience managing analytical projects or substantial workstreams, including defining tasks, coordinating contributors, monitoring budget and schedule, reviewing work, and delivering client-ready outputs.

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and demonstrated ability to work with large, complex datasets; proficiency in AI tools.

Preferred qualifications

  • Master’s degree in a relevant quantitative, energy, economics, engineering, policy, or business discipline.

  • Experience with nodal or network-based natural gas market modeling such as GPCM, supply-demand equilibrium modeling, production economics, pipeline flow and capacity analysis, or basis forecasting.

  • Experience calibrating models to historical data, conducting backcasts, validating outputs, documenting assumptions, and implementing repeatable model QA/QC processes.

  • Experience with one or more of the following: pipeline expansion and market-need studies; utility gas supply and integrated resource planning; storage valuation or optimization; midstream asset valuation; LNG market analysis; power-gas coordination; regulatory proceedings; or large-load/data-center gas supply assessments.

  • Working knowledge of Python, R, SQL, VBA, statistical software, databases, data visualization, automated analytical workflows, Claude, and other AI tools.

  • Experience supporting proposals, client development, presentations, publications, or other market-facing activities.

  • Ability to learn a proprietary modeling platform quickly and become proficient in running, maintaining, troubleshooting, interpreting, and quality-checking GMM.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical methods and results to both technical and nontechnical audiences.

  • Demonstrated attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and ability to work independently in a collaborative consulting environment.

Working at ICF

ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future.

We can only solve the world’s toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer. Together, our employees are empowered to share their expertise and collaborate with others to achieve personal and professional goals. For more information, please read our EEO policy.

We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Work Authorization and Sponsorship

All candidates must be authorized to work in the United States. This position is not eligible for new H-1B visa sponsorship by ICF. Candidates who currently hold valid work authorization may be considered for a change of employer petition, subject to company policy and applicable immigration requirements.

Reasonable Accommodations

Reasonable Accommodations are available, including, but not limited to, for disabled veterans, individuals with disabilities, and individuals with sincerely held religious beliefs, in all phases of the application and employment process. To request an accommodation, please email Candidateaccommodation@icf.com and we will be happy to assist. All information you provide will be kept confidential and will be used only to the extent required to provide needed reasonable accommodations. 

Read more about workplace discrimination rights or our benefit offerings which are included in the Transparency in (Benefits) Coverage Act.

Bot and Third-Party Applications

Please note that this application must be submitted directly by the applicant for consideration. Failure to do so may result in the application being excluded for consideration. Applicants needing an accommodation for disability or religious purposes in connection with the application process should contact Candidateaccommodation@icf.com for assistance.

Candidate AI Usage Policy

At ICF, we are committed to ensuring a fair interview process for all candidates based on their own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate or assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is not permitted. This policy is in place to maintain the integrity and authenticity of the interview process. 

However, we understand that some candidates may require accommodation that involves the use of AI. If such an accommodation is needed, candidates are instructed to contact us in advance at candidateaccommodation@icf.com. We are dedicated to providing the necessary support to ensure that all candidates have an equal opportunity to succeed.

There are multiple factors that are considered in determining final pay for a position, including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, certifications and competencies that align to the specified role, geographic location, education and certifications as well as contract provisions regarding labor categories that are specific to the position.

item.title: Head of Research at The Carboun Institute (remote in MENA Region/European timezone)
item.description: The Carboun Institute is the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region’s first and only independent climate and energy policy think tank.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Carboun Institute is the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region’s first and only independent climate and energy policy think tank. Established in 2025 as a Dutch foundation (Stichting), the Institute is dedicated to driving change through evidence-based research, policy analysis, and policy advocacy. Our work centers on accelerating the energy transition and green industrialization, and enhancing climate resilience and adaptation, by leveraging finance in a just and sustainable way, and strengthening regional climate diplomacy and cooperation.

The Carboun Institute aims to build its organizational leadership and to hire a Head of Research to lead its research activities.

Position Overview

The Carboun Institute is looking for a motivated, technically-competent, and policy-driven expert to lead its research work with a focus on energy transition and green industry.

This position offers a unique opportunity to shape the MENA region’s decarbonization and green industrialization agenda by combining technical analysis, scenario modeling, and policy design. It aims to provide actionable strategies for reducing carbon emissions across energy and industrial sectors, with a particular focus on accelerating renewable energy deployment, advancing low-carbon fuels such as green hydrogen, and enabling industrial decarbonization.

The position is a hybrid one, combining the candidate’s own applied research with oversight of a number of projects. The successful candidate will translate complex technical and economic insights into policy recommendations for governments and industry stakeholders, while collaborating closely with the Head of Programs to ensure delivery and quality of projects.

The ideal candidate will possess strong leadership experience to oversee and direct existing and upcoming projects covering energy transition and industrial decarbonization including iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals.

Key Responsibilities

Research Leadership

• Design, lead, and implement applied research on energy transition, renewable energy deployment, low-carbon technologies, industrial and sectoral decarbonization pathways for iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals across the MENA region.

• Integrate energy, industrial, and sectoral analyses into comprehensive national decarbonization pathways, including energy and industrial decarbonization, identifying least-cost and high-impact mitigation options.

• Assess how decarbonization pathways interact with economic diversification and industrial competitiveness, with an emphasis on opportunities for energy transition and green industrialization.

• Identify strategic research priorities aligned with the Carboun Institute’s mission and emerging regional policy needs.

• Ensure methodological rigor, technical accuracy, relevance, and policy applicability of all research outputs, and assist in the implementation of relevant Carboun Institute policies and processes.

• Develop partnerships with academia, industry, and policy institutions to strengthen collaborative research and knowledge exchange.

• Contribute to organizational learning by capturing and sharing insights, lessons, and best practices.

• Contribute to the organization’s convening power by helping develop its network and expanding its contacts database.

Policy Advice and Support

Translate technical and economic findings into actionable policy recommendations for governments, utilities, and industry stakeholders.

• Develop and evaluate policy instruments for deep decarbonization focusing on industrial decarbonization such as carbon pricing, regulatory frameworks, and financing mechanisms.

• Analyze industrial decarbonization pathways focusing on iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals and assess how they can enable sustainable economic diversification, technology innovation, and green industrialization, positioning MENA economies competitively in low-carbon value chains.

• Lead or contribute to the preparation of policy briefs, white papers, and strategic roadmaps on energy transition, decarbonization policy, and green industry development focusing on iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals.

• Conduct comparative analysis of international best practices in energy transition policy and industrial decarbonization, and assess their applicability to MENA’s political economy and industrial context.

• Provide expert advice and thought leadership in national and regional policy dialogues on energy transition, decarbonization, and sustainable industry focusing on iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals.

Strategic Engagement

• Represent the Carboun Institute in convenings, conferences, and fora within the MENA region and internationally.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including government agencies, private sector partners, donors, and civil society organizations.

• Identify and pursue strategic opportunities for expansion, partnerships, and funding aligned with the Institute’s mission, vision, and core values.

• Support the Executive Director in donor engagement, proposal development, and reporting.

Publication and Dissemination

• Lead the research for high-impact publications, including policy briefs, reports, analysis papers, working papers, and commentary articles including on industrial decarbonization.

• Deliver high-quality stakeholder convenings aligned with the Institute’s objectives.

• Ensure effective dissemination of research findings through the Institute’s communication channels, media outreach, and public events.

• Contribute to thought leadership through participation in public discussions, expert panels, and media commentary.

• Uphold Carboun’s standards for clarity, accessibility, and influence in all written and public communications.

Qualifications

Essential

  • Master’s degree in a relevant field including

    • Energy policy or energy systems

    • Environmental policy or environmental science

    • Sustainability studies

    • Engineering (especially chemical, mechanical, or industrial)

    • Public policy (with a climate, energy, or industrial development focus)

  • Minimum of 10 years of energy and climate research and/or policy experience

  • Experience in energy transition and industrial decarbonization projects including iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals

  • Demonstrated understanding of the issues surrounding energy transition in the MENA region

  • Deep familiarity with renewable energy systems, particularly in desert environment

  • Demonstrated understanding of the issues relating to industrial decarbonization in the region and knowledge of the MENA region’s industrial landscape and political economy

  • Demonstrated understanding of iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals

  • Demonstrated track record of publications in relevant fields including iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals

  • Strong research and analytical skills and ability to translate technical concepts into policy recommendations

  • Excellent writing and communication skills

  • Proven ability to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders, including government, industry and academia

  • Network of contacts in the MENA energy and industrial sectors and/or climate policy sphere

  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly within the MENA region and internationally

Desirable

  • Ability to speak and write in English and Arabic at professional level without heavy reliance on AI.

  • PhD in a related field (e.g., energy systems, decarbonization technologies, industrial policy)

  • Specialized coursework or certificates in:

    • Renewable energy systems or hydrogen economy

    • Industrial decarbonization

Competencies

  • Technical competence and an understanding of issues relating to energy transition and industrial decarbonization including iron and steel, cement and concrete, methane, and chemicals.

  • Strategic thinking with ability to identify key leverage points for energy system transformation, market integration, and green industrialization.

  • Collaborative approach to work, with ability to integrate perspectives from various disciplines

  • Diplomatic skills for engaging with government, industry, and civil society stakeholders

  • Independence and initiative to drive forward research agenda

  • Commitment to climate action and sustainable development

Working Arrangements

  • This is a full-time equivalent role with renewal contingent on performance and funding.

  • Location is negotiable with a preference to candidates in the MENA Region/ European timezone.

  • Compensation is competitive and commensurate with experience, qualifications, and location.

  • The Head of Research will coordinate with the Executive Director and Head of Programs and oversee the work of research fellows, analysts, and consultants leading different projects.

  • The role requires regular travel (within the MENA region and internationally) for stakeholder engagement, field research, conferences, and partner meetings

Application Process

Qualified candidates are invited to submit:

1. A detailed CV highlighting relevant research and policy experience

2. A motivation letter (personally written) explaining your interest in the position and alignment with the Institute’s mission

3. Writing samples demonstrating your analytical and communication skills, including work published in 2023 and before.

4. Names and contact information of two professional references

Applications should be submitted through the application form. If you face technical challenges please let us know by emailing careers@carboun.com with the subject line “Head of Research”.

Apply using the Application Form

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Due to the large volume of applications expected we cannot guarantee a response to all applicants.

For more information about the Carboun Institute and our work, please visit our website and follow our social media outlets

Link to job posting: https://www.carboun.com/careers/head-of-research
